advances: A uniform second-moment bound for normalized closed-halfspace depth on complete finite log-affine lattice tables would imply an original-weight logarithmic hitting bound with coefficient \(a/(2\sqrt5)\), and an actual mixed-integer depth bound with coefficient \(a/(12\sqrt5)\). The proof integrates every logarithmic cutoff. It reuses only the unconditional epigraph construction, approximation estimates, and separation inequality proved in accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162, and proves the new squared-integral limits. The second-moment hypothesis is explicitly unproved. Uniform lattice-convex tables and arbitrary one-dimensional probability laws satisfy the stated elementary second-moment calibrations unconditionally.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The complete-table, convex-roof, original logarithmic hitting, and same-table root-comparison inputs are the declared accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc. The exact epigraph construction, uniform closed-halfspace and depth errors, vertical Lipschitz estimate, tail depth estimate, and separation comparison are the unconditional portions of the proof of declared accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162 identified above. The actual-body depth consumer and attainment are from declared accepted fact 7fa5a28fe1ac6893. Declared accepted fact 001a95dc6616c6b9 is used only to identify the failed first-moment premise. The new squared-integral convergence, exponential integral, and calibrations are proved analytically here. The second-moment hypothesis is explicit and unproved; no archived response or numerical experiment is a proof premise.
proof:
We first prove (1), assuming (H2). Accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc supplies the convex roof

\[
\widehat\phi(x)=
\min_{\substack{\lambda_{\mathbf I}\ge0,\ \sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}=1\\
\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=x}}
\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}
\qquad(x\in P).
\]

It is convex and continuous on all of \(P\) in its relative topology, takes values in \([0,B]\), and equals \(\phi_{\mathbf I}\) at every \(\mathbf I\in D\). These assertions apply also when \(P\) has rank zero or intermediate rank.

Use precisely the epigraph measure from equation (6) in the proof of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162:

\[
\mu(A')=w_{\max}\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}
\int_{\phi_{\mathbf I}}^\infty
\mathbf 1_{A'}(\mathbf I,t)e^{-t}\,dt
\qquad(A'\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\text{ Borel}).
\tag{5}
\]

Its total mass is \(W\). In particular, at every original base site,

\[
w_{\max}e^{-(\phi_{\mathbf I}+L)}\,dL
=w_{\mathbf I}e^{-L}\,dL
\qquad(L\ge0).
\tag{6}
\]

The factor \(w_{\max}\) is retained throughout. No probability normalization, selected-subtable mass, or change of original source capacities is substituted for \(W\).

For any finite measure \(\nu\) below, let \(\tau_\nu(p)=\inf_{H\ni p}\nu(H)\), over closed halfspaces in its ambient space. This extends the same depth notation used in (H2). We use only the unconditional construction and estimates in the proof of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162: its equations (7)-(9), (12), (13), (16), and (19). Their proofs do not assume that fact's first-moment hypothesis. We do not use its first-moment conclusions.

Fix \(R>B\), and let \(\mu_R\) be the restriction of (5) to heights at most \(R\). Put \(W_R=W-|D|w_{\max}e^{-R}>0\). For every integer \(m\ge1\), the complete epigraph approximation from equations (7)-(9) of that accepted fact is

\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_{R,m}
&=\{(x,s):x\in P,\ m\widehat\phi(x)\le s\le mR\},\\
Q_{R,m}\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1}
&=\{(\mathbf I,k):\mathbf I\in D,\ k\in\mathbb Z,\quad
\phi_{\mathbf I}\le k/m\le R\},\\
\mu_{R,m}
&=\frac{w_{\max}}m\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}
\sum_{\substack{k\in\mathbb Z\\\phi_{\mathbf I}\le k/m\le R}}
e^{-k/m}\delta_{(\mathbf I,k/m)},&
W_{R,m}&=\mu_{R,m}(\mathbb R^{n+1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]

The set \(Q_{R,m}\) is compact and convex, and the displayed lattice support is complete because \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=D\) and \(\widehat\phi(\mathbf I)=\phi_{\mathbf I}\). A minimum-potential site has \(\phi_{\mathbf I}=0\), so \((\mathbf I,0)\) is always present. Before the invertible scaling \((x,s)\mapsto(x,s/m)\), its weights are \(v_{\mathbf I,k}=(w_{\max}/m)e^{-k/m}\), with affine logarithm \(\log w_{\max}-\log m-k/m\). Containing closed halfspaces correspond bijectively under that scaling, preserving atomic masses and depths. Thus (H2) applies in ambient integer dimension \(N=n+1\), without a rank reduction or a lattice-index factor.

For an unnormalized positive table \(v\) of total mass \(V\), the normalization \(p=v/V\) gives \(\tau_p=\tau_v/V\), so (H2) reads \(\sum_{\mathbf z}v_{\mathbf z}\tau_v(\mathbf z)^2\ge a^2 4^{-N}V^3\). Applying this identity to (7) is the only use of (H2) in the transfer proof. It gives

\[
\int\tau_{\mu_{R,m}}^2\,d\mu_{R,m}
\ge a^2\,4^{-(n+1)}W_{R,m}^3.
\tag{8}
\]

We now prove that the square integral on the left converges to its counterpart for \(\mu_R\). Equation (12) in the proof of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162 supplies

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{H\text{ closed halfspace}}
|\mu_{R,m}(H)-\mu_R(H)|
&\le\varepsilon_m,&
\varepsilon_m&=\frac{3|D|w_{\max}}m,\\
|W_{R,m}-W_R|&\le\varepsilon_m,&
\sup_{p\in\mathbb R^{n+1}}
|\tau_{\mu_{R,m}}(p)-\tau_{\mu_R}(p)|
&\le\varepsilon_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

These estimates include mesh points on interval endpoints and halfspace boundaries that contain entire vertical fibers. Equation (13) of the same proof gives, for each \(\mathbf J\in D\) and all real \(t,t'\),

\[
|\tau_{\mu_R}(\mathbf J,t)-\tau_{\mu_R}(\mathbf J,t')|
\le |D|w_{\max}|t-t'|.
\tag{10}
\]

In particular these depth functions are measurable and lie between zero and \(W_R\le W\). It follows from (10) and \(|u^2-v^2|=|u-v||u+v|\) that \(t\mapsto\tau_{\mu_R}(\mathbf J,t)^2\) is Lipschitz with constant at most \(2W|D|w_{\max}\). Since \(e^{-t}\) is bounded by one and is Lipschitz with constant one for \(t\ge0\), the function \(t\mapsto e^{-t}\tau_{\mu_R}(\mathbf J,t)^2\) on \([\phi_{\mathbf J},R]\) is bounded by \(W^2\) and is Lipschitz with constant at most \(W^2+2W|D|w_{\max}\).

Here is an explicit endpoint-inclusive Riemann bound. For any bounded Lipschitz function \(f\) on \([u,v]\) and integer \(m\ge1\),

\[
\left|\frac1m\sum_{\substack{k\in\mathbb Z\\ k/m\in[u,v]}}f(k/m)
-\int_u^v f(t)\,dt\right|
\le
\frac{\operatorname{Lip}(f)(v-u)}{2m}
+\frac{3\|f\|_\infty}{m}.
\tag{11}
\]

If there is no mesh point, \(v-u<1/m\) and the integral alone obeys this bound. Otherwise let \(r=\lceil mu\rceil\) and \(s=\lfloor mv\rfloor\). On each full cell \([k/m,(k+1)/m]\) for \(r\le k<s\), its left-endpoint sum differs from its integral by at most \(\operatorname{Lip}(f)/(2m^2)\). The final included sample \(f(s/m)/m\) contributes at most \(\|f\|_\infty/m\). The two pieces \([u,r/m]\) and \([s/m,v]\) have total length at most \(2/m\). Adding the bounds proves (11), including \(r=s\) and exact endpoint equalities.

Applying (11) to the preceding squared-depth integrands, and summing over the finite original set \(D\) with factor \(w_{\max}\), proves

\[
\int\tau_{\mu_R}^2\,d\mu_{R,m}
\longrightarrow \int\tau_{\mu_R}^2\,d\mu_R
\qquad(m\to\infty).
\tag{12}
\]

The replacement of the depth in this mesh integral is controlled separately. From (9), \(0\le\tau_{\mu_{R,m}}\le W_{R,m}\), and \(0\le\tau_{\mu_R}\le W_R\), we have

\[
\left|\int\tau_{\mu_{R,m}}^2\,d\mu_{R,m}
-\int\tau_{\mu_R}^2\,d\mu_{R,m}\right|
\le\varepsilon_m(W_{R,m}+W_R)W_{R,m}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]

Also \(W_{R,m}\to W_R\) by (9). Therefore (8), (12), and (13) imply

\[
\int\tau_{\mu_R}^2\,d\mu_R
\ge a^2\,4^{-(n+1)}W_R^3.
\tag{14}
\]

We next remove the top cutoff. Equation (16) in the proof of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162 applies to exactly (5) and (7): the nonnegative measure \(\mu-\mu_R\) has total mass \(\eta_R=|D|w_{\max}e^{-R}\), and

\[
0\le\tau_\mu(p)-\tau_{\mu_R}(p)\le\eta_R
\qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{n+1}).
\tag{15}
\]

Thus \(\tau_\mu\) is measurable on every supporting fiber, as a uniform limit of the measurable depth functions in (10). All depths involved are bounded by \(W\). Decomposing the difference of integrals, using \(\mu_R\le\mu\) and (15), gives the new squared truncation bound

\[
\begin{aligned}
0&\le
\int\tau_\mu^2\,d\mu-\int\tau_{\mu_R}^2\,d\mu_R\\
&=\int(\tau_\mu^2-\tau_{\mu_R}^2)\,d\mu_R
+\int\tau_\mu^2\,d(\mu-\mu_R)\\
&\le 2W\eta_RW_R+W^2\eta_R
\le3W^2\eta_R\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]

Since \(W_R\to W\), letting \(R\to\infty\) in (14) proves

\[
\int\tau_\mu^2\,d\mu
\ge a^2\,4^{-(n+1)}W^3.
\tag{17}
\]

For the upper bound we use equation (19) in the proof of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162, with exactly the measure (5), the original weights \(w\), and the cutoff families in this statement. It is the unconditional separation inequality

\[
\tau_\mu(\mathbf J,\phi_{\mathbf J}+L)
\le m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)
\le (1+L)\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\qquad(\mathbf J\in D,\ L\ge0).
\tag{18}
\]

Its separating halfspace strictly excludes every entire epigraph fiber in the complement of a minimum hitting set, so the remaining mass is at most the sum of the full original weights of the hit fibers. The proof there covers vertical separating halfspaces, equality graph sites, and equality in \(G_E\le L\). This is why (18) applies to the original integral hitting mass at every cutoff without a boundary deletion or a truncated capacity. The finite cutoff attainment and all-support conventions are those of accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc.

Using the exact variable change (6) and squaring the nonnegative bound (18), we obtain

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int\tau_\mu^2\,d\mu
&=\sum_{\mathbf J\in D}w_{\mathbf J}
\int_0^\infty
\tau_\mu(\mathbf J,\phi_{\mathbf J}+L)^2e^{-L}\,dL\\
&\le
\bigl(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\bigr)^2
W\int_0^\infty(1+L)^2e^{-L}\,dL\\
&=5W\bigl(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\bigr)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]

For the final equality, \(\int_0^\infty e^{-L}\,dL=1\); integration by parts gives \(\int_0^\infty Le^{-L}\,dL=1\) and \(\int_0^\infty L^2e^{-L}\,dL=2\). The endpoint terms vanish because \(L^je^{-L}\to0\) as \(L\to\infty\) for \(j=1,2\). Expanding \((1+L)^2\) therefore gives \(1+2\cdot1+2=5\). The integral in (19) uses all \(L\ge0\), including costs that grow with the integer dimension.

Combining (17) and (19), dividing by \(5W>0\), and taking the nonnegative square root gives

\[
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\ge\frac{a}{\sqrt5}\,2^{-(n+1)}W
=\frac{a}{2\sqrt5}\,2^{-n}W,
\]

which is (1).

Now consider an actual body \(C\) from the statement. If \(W=\mathcal H_d(S)=0\), (2) holds at every point of the assumed nonempty \(S\). Suppose \(W>0\). Accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc establishes global extendability of the actual complete volume table, including all empty, lower-dimensional, and boundary fibers. It consequently supplies exactly the lattice-complete positive support and the full convex-admissibility hypotheses used above, with the original ambient integer dimension \(n\) and total volume \(W\).

For clarity, the original root cost is

\[
L_E=\log\frac{w_{\mathbf J}}
{\left(\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}
w_{\mathbf I}^{1/d}\right)^d}.
\]

Defining \(m_d(\mathbf J,L;w)\) and \(\mathcal B_d^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\) by the same hitting definitions with \(L_E\le L\) in place of \(G_E\le L\) gives the integral root score of accepted fact 7fa5a28fe1ac6893. Equation (4) of accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc gives \(m_d(\mathbf J,L;w)\ge m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)\) at every center and cutoff, with identical original capacities, and hence \(\mathcal B_d^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\ge\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\). Equation (4) of accepted fact 7fa5a28fe1ac6893 gives the attained actual-body depth bound. Therefore

\[
\max_{\mathbf y\in S}h_S(\mathbf y)
\ge\frac16\mathcal B_d^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\ge\frac16\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\ge\frac{a}{12\sqrt5}\,2^{-n}W.
\tag{20}
\]

Select an attaining point before the arbitrary containing closed halfspace. This proves (2) with the locked quantifier order. Zero-volume fibers are still part of the original body and set \(S\); their zero contributions to volume have not been replaced by positive artificial capacities. No rank assumption or dependence on \(d\) entered the coefficient. Decreasing the coefficient to the stated \(c_0\) gives its required strict range.

We prove the calibrations independently of (H2). For the uniform table, let \(K=|A|\), and for each \(\mathbf j\in A\) put

\[
r_A(\mathbf j)=
\bigl|\{\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^N:
\mathbf j+\mathbf v\in A,\ \mathbf j-\mathbf v\in A\}\bigr|.
\]

The reflected support about \(\mathbf j\) consists of the center and antipodal pairs. Every closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf j\) contains at least one endpoint from each antipodal pair and contains the center. Thus \(\tau_p(\mathbf j)\ge r_A(\mathbf j)/(2K)\); boundary pairs contained on both sides only increase the halfspace mass.

For each parity class \(\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^N\), let \(K_\epsilon\) be its number of points in \(A\). The map \((\mathbf j,\mathbf v)\mapsto(\mathbf j+\mathbf v,\mathbf j-\mathbf v)\) is a bijection from the pairs counted by \(\sum_{\mathbf j}r_A(\mathbf j)\) onto ordered equal-parity pairs from \(A\). Indeed, an equal-parity pair has integer midpoint and integer half-difference; its midpoint belongs to \(Q\) by convexity and hence belongs to the complete support \(A\). Consequently

\[
\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}r_A(\mathbf j)
=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^N}K_\epsilon^2
\ge 2^{-N}K^2.
\]

The inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz applied to all \(2^N\) parity classes, including empty classes. It holds without a full-rank assumption. Therefore

\[
\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)
\ge\frac1{2K^2}\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}r_A(\mathbf j)
\ge2^{-N-1},\qquad
\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)^2
\ge\left(\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)\right)^2
\ge\frac14\,4^{-N}.
\]

The second inequality is again Cauchy-Schwarz, using \(\sum p_{\mathbf j}=1\). This proves (3), including a one-point or lower-rank support.

For (4), let \(F(x)=\nu((-\infty,x])\) and \(F_-(x)=\nu((-\infty,x))\). Since closed halfspaces in one dimension are closed rays, their minimum mass among rays containing \(x\) is
\(\tau_\nu(x)=\min\{F(x),1-F_-(x)\}\). This includes the atom at \(x\) in both possible rays.

For \(0<u<1\), define the quantile \(q(u)=\inf\{x:F(x)\ge u\}\). The limits of \(F\) at the two infinities make \(q(u)\) finite. Monotonicity and right-continuity of \(F\) imply \(F_-(q(u))\le u\le F(q(u))\) and \(q(u)\le x\) if and only if \(u\le F(x)\). The latter equivalence shows that the pushforward of Lebesgue probability on \((0,1)\) under \(q\) is \(\nu\), because its mass on every ray \((-\infty,x]\) equals \(F(x)\). The former inequalities give
\(\min\{u,1-u\}\le\tau_\nu(q(u))\). Squaring and integrating yields

\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\tau_\nu(x)^2\,d\nu(x)
=\int_0^1\tau_\nu(q(u))^2\,du
\ge\int_0^1\min\{u,1-u\}^2\,du
=2\int_0^{1/2}u^2\,du
=\frac1{12}.
\]

All functions here are measurable because they are formed from monotone distribution or quantile functions. For a finite law on sorted atoms with masses \(p_i\), the same argument is exactly the interval calculation with \(s_i=\sum_{j<i}p_j\), depth \(\min\{s_i+p_i,1-s_i\}\), and \(u\in[s_i,s_i+p_i]\). Thus it retains all atomic equality cases in the finite-table calibration.

Finally, accepted fact 001a95dc6616c6b9 disproves the universal first-moment hypothesis used in the conditional statement of accepted fact 07e7c8b5638ba162: its complete finite log-affine tables have \(2^N\sum p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)\to0\). That false hypothesis has not been assumed anywhere above. A first-moment bound \(\sum p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)\ge b2^{-N}\) would imply (H2) with \(a=b\) by Cauchy-Schwarz. In the reverse direction, the elementary inequality \(\tau_p^2\le\tau_p\) yields from (H2) only the bound \(\sum p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)\ge a^2 4^{-N}\), which has a different scale. The cited first-moment counterexample estimate therefore does not establish failure of (H2). No assertion that (H2) holds for arbitrary log-affine weights in arbitrary dimension is proved here; (1), (2), and the resulting locked-target consequence remain conditional.
statement:
Consider the following hypothesis, denoted (H2). There is one absolute constant \(a>0\) such that, for every integer \(N\ge1\), every compact convex \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) with nonempty \(A=Q\cap\mathbb Z^N\), and every \(\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^N\), the probability weights

\[
p_{\mathbf z}=\frac{\exp(\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf z)}
{\sum_{\mathbf x\in A}\exp(\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x)}
\quad(\mathbf z\in A),\qquad
\tau_p(\mathbf z)=
\inf_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ a closed halfspace}\\
\mathbf z\in H}}\sum_{\mathbf x\in A\cap H}p_{\mathbf x}
\]

satisfy

\[
\sum_{\mathbf z\in A}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^2
\ge a^2\,4^{-N}.
\tag{H2}
\]

There is no full-dimensionality assumption on \(Q\) or \(A\). Hypothesis (H2) is a premise of the conclusions below, not an assertion proved here.

For an integer \(n\ge1\), let \(D\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, put \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\), and assume \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=D\). Let \(w_{\mathbf I}>0\) for \(\mathbf I\in D\), with table value zero at every integer site outside \(D\). Use the notation of accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc:

\[
W=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I},\qquad
w_{\max}=\max_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I},\qquad
\phi_{\mathbf I}=\log\frac{w_{\max}}{w_{\mathbf I}},\qquad
B=\max_{\mathbf I\in D}\phi_{\mathbf I}.
\]

Assume full convex-admissibility: for every \(\mathbf J\in D\) and every coefficient vector \((\lambda_{\mathbf I})_{\mathbf I\in D}\) with nonnegative entries, sum one, and \(\sum_{\mathbf I}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=\mathbf J\), one has \(\phi_{\mathbf J}\le\sum_{\mathbf I}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}\). The scalar \(B\) continues to mean the maximum potential, not an optimized score.

For each \(\mathbf J\in D\), let \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\) consist of the nonempty affinely independent subsets \(E\subseteq D\) with \(\mathbf J\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}E\). Denote their unique positive barycentric coefficients by \(\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}\). Retain the logarithmic costs and original-weight integral hitting definitions of accepted fact 488f0a583886b5fc:

\[
\begin{aligned}
G_E&=\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{E,\mathbf I}\phi_{\mathbf I}
-\phi_{\mathbf J},&
\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}^{\log}(L)
&=\{E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}:G_E\le L\},\\
m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)
&=\min_{\substack{F\subseteq D\\
F\cap E\ne\varnothing\ (E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}^{\log}(L))}}
\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}w_{\mathbf I},&
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
&=\max_{\mathbf J\in D,\ L\ge0}
\frac{m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)}{1+L}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Every support cost at the cutoff is included. The singleton at \(\mathbf J\) is included, every selected source is charged its full original weight, and the same hitting values result if arbitrary finite barycentric supports are allowed, as established in that accepted fact. Then (H2) implies

\[
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
\ge \frac{a}{2\sqrt5}\,2^{-n}W.
\tag{1}
\]

Consequently, assuming (H2), for every \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and every convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\), with \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\) and \(S=C\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing\), there is one \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf y^\star\) satisfies

\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\ge
\frac{a}{12\sqrt5}\,2^{-n}\mathcal H_d(S).
\tag{2}
\]

Here the table used in the positive-volume case is the actual complete fiber table \(w_{\mathbf I}=\mathcal L^d(C_{\mathbf I})\), with \(C_{\mathbf I}=\{\mathbf y:(\mathbf I,\mathbf y)\in C\}\), and \(W=\mathcal H_d(S)\). Empty and lower-dimensional original fibers have weight zero. With \(h_S(\mathbf y)=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf y}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), (2) is equivalently the asserted lower bound for the depth of this one point. In particular (H2) would prove the locked conjecture with the absolute constant \(c_0=\min\{a/(12\sqrt5),1/(2e)\}\in(0,1/e)\).

Two calibrations hold without assuming (H2). For every uniform table on a nonempty \(A=Q\cap\mathbb Z^N\) as above,

\[
\sum_{\mathbf z\in A}p_{\mathbf z}\tau_p(\mathbf z)^2
\ge\frac14\,4^{-N};
\tag{3}
\]

thus the uniform class satisfies (H2) with \(a=1/2\). For every Borel probability law \(\nu\) on \(\mathbb R\), writing \(\tau_\nu(x)=\inf_{H\ni x}\nu(H)\) for its normalized closed-halfspace depth,

\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\tau_\nu(x)^2\,d\nu(x)\ge\frac1{12}.
\tag{4}
\]

This includes every finite one-dimensional lattice law, with arbitrary positive weights and no log-concavity requirement. Neither calibration asserts (H2) for general weights in arbitrary dimension.
